newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. recommends Iraqi oil deal for another 6 months.
newsitem.headline: U.N. recommends Iraqi oil deal for another 6 months.

text.p: U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan on Monday recommended a six-month renewal of the "oil-for-food" deal for Iraq, U.N. officials said.

In a report to the Security Council Annan said the plan, which expires on June 7, should be extended. The current deal calls for $2 billion worth of oil sales over six months so Baghdad can buy food and medicine for its people, suffering from U.N. trade sanctions imposed in August 1990 when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.

"In light of the experience gained in the implementation of the programme in the past six months and bearing in mind the continuing humanitarian crisis in Iraq, I recommend the renewal of the programme for a further period of six months," said the official quoting from the report.

The Security Council must still approve a rollover of the deal which went into effect on Dec. 10. The United States has not given its official position yet although U.S. sources believe Washington will agree to the renewal.
About two-thirds of the monies are for humanitarian supplies, with the remainder earmarked for compensation of Gulf War victims and the costs of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.
Iraq has complained frequently that the council's procedures had prevented the supplies from reaching the country within a reasonable period of time while oil sales moved quickly.
